html:
Daniel arap Moi was the second president of Kenya, ruling from the death of Jomo Kenyatta in 1978 until 2002.

A Kalenjin teacher, he was vice president under Kenyatta. In 1982 parliament made Kenya a one-party state by law, and an attempted coup by air force officers in August that year was crushed. Opponents were jailed and tortured, some in the cells of Nyayo House.

Pressure from donors and protesters forced a return to multiparty politics in 1991. Moi won the elections of 1992 and 1997, marked by ethnic clashes. Corruption, such as the Goldenberg scandal, grew. He stepped down in 2002 when the opposition under Mwai Kibaki won, a peaceful handover in Kenya before the crisis of 2007.
sum: Daniel arap Moi was the second president of Kenya, ruling from the death of Jomo Kenyatta in 1978 until 2002.
